summary: A BBN list of the monthly preventive maintenance times for each IMP and TIP, mostly timed to match maintenance on the hosts at the same site. It says rescheduling would be announced through the TIP news and in notes to technical liaisons. Permanent changes would appear as RFCs.

plainLanguage.summary: A calendar showing when each network box gets its regular check-up, chosen so the people who use it are not surprised.

subtitle: A monthly schedule of network equipment maintenance times.

tldr.problem: Network equipment needs regular maintenance, but coordinators must find times that do not disrupt users at the attached sites.
tldr.mechanism: BBN published a monthly preventive maintenance schedule coordinating each IMP and TIP with the hosts at the same location.
tldr.outcome: Sites could plan around maintenance windows, and any permanent changes would be announced via RFC.

today: RFC 445 documents the operational procedures of the early ARPANET. It is not a protocol and has been superseded by modern network operations practices.

sections.title: The Maintenance Schedule
sections.content:
RFC 445 publishes the preventive maintenance schedule for the ARPANET's IMPs (Interface Message Processors, the network routers) and TIPs (Terminal Interface Processors, which let terminals join the network). Maintenance is scheduled monthly, and each machine is normally serviced at the same time each month.

Wherever possible, the maintenance time is chosen to coincide with the scheduled maintenance of the hosts at the same site, so that disruption to users is minimized.
sections.plainLanguage: Each network box gets fixed once a month at a time that the people running it already expect to be offline.

sections.title: Announcing Changes
sections.content: Occasional rescheduling is necessary due to network connectivity issues or other operational concerns. The RFC explains that temporary rescheduling would be announced via two mechanisms: the TIP NEWS and a Journal note to Technical Liaisons. Any permanent changes to the schedule would be announced via RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: If the date changes, network managers announce it through newsletters and official messages.

sections.title: The Time Slots
sections.content: The schedule lists maintenance windows for all sites, grouped by week and day of the month. For example, the first Monday of each month shows BBN IMP's maintenance slot, from 08:30 to 11:30 Eastern Time. Each site has a specific day and time, and where multiple machines are at one location, their maintenance is staggered throughout the month to avoid simultaneous outages.
sections.plainLanguage: The schedule says which machines get fixed on which days and what time they will be down.
